scenes.visual: melting point vs chain length and cis kinks
scenes.narration: Two structural features decide whether a fatty acid is solid or liquid. First, chain length. Among saturated fatty acids, longer chains pack more tightly and melt higher. Lauric acid at 12 carbons melts near 44 degrees, palmitic at 16 near 63, stearic at 18 near 70. Second, saturation. One cis double bond kinks the chain and breaks the packing. Stearic acid is a solid. Oleic acid with a single double bond melts at just 13 degrees and pours as an oil. More double bonds drop it further still. This is the whole chapter in one graph.

scenes.narration: A triacylglycerol's melting point depends entirely on which fatty acids hang off the glycerol. Tripalmitin, three saturated 16-carbon chains, packs tightly and is solid at body temperature. Triolein, three unsaturated 18:1 chains, stays liquid even at room temperature. A mixed triacylglycerol, one saturated chain and two unsaturated, lands in between, semi-solid around body temperature, which is the profile of most natural body fat. Cells fine-tune the physical state of their fat by choosing which fatty acid goes to which position on glycerol.

scenes.narration: Fatty acid saturation is the main dial a cell turns to tune membrane fluidity. Saturated tails pack tightly through van der Waals contacts, raising the transition temperature and pushing the membrane toward a gel. Unsaturated tails kink and create packing defects, keeping the membrane fluid even when it is cold. The E. coli example is elegant: chilled to 20 degrees, the bacterium makes more unsaturated fatty acids to hold its fluidity steady. Tuning composition to keep viscosity constant as the environment changes is homeoviscous adaptation.

scenes.narration: Cholesterol is a fluidity buffer, a thermostat. At low temperature, it inserts between the tails and disrupts tight packing, preventing the membrane from gelling. At high temperature, it restrains the same tails, keeping the membrane from becoming too fluid. On a graph of fluidity against temperature, cholesterol flattens the sharp phase transition into a broad, gentle curve, giving the cell a stable operating range across a wide window. One molecule, two opposite jobs.
